contradicting_evidence: Positive 24h BTC and ETH returns and broad USD advances could develop into a more coherent upside trend if participation persists.
Conversely, simultaneous negative ETF flows and contracting stablecoin supply could overwhelm the rebound and produce a clearer downside path.
Small hourly price and open-interest declines do not yet establish either decisive rejection or durable stabilization.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: A contested rebound/retest environment is more defensible than smooth continuation. Positive participation leaves room for rebound extensions, while weak immediate flow confirmation and the liquidity backdrop keep renewed tests lower credible. The balance is downside-sensitive, but net direction over 72h remains unresolved.
falsification_conditions: Persistent price gains, strengthening ETH/BTC, broader BTC-relative outperformance and improving settled flows would invalidate the mixed case toward an upside trend.
Persistent price losses with shrinking breadth and continued negative settled flows would invalidate the mixed case toward a downside trend.
missing_evidence: Comparable repeated breadth observations showing persistence rather than a single positive cross-section.
New settled flow observations and multi-session spot-demand confirmation.
A sustained ETH/BTC sequence and evidence that participation extends beyond the observed Top-100 windows.
supporting_evidence: Positive breadth and 24h asset returns coexist with ask-heavy sampled depth and weak BTC hourly taker buying, supporting competing rebound and retest paths.
The mid-alt proxy has constructive participation, but broad relative leadership is limited: only 40 of 100 constituents in the older snapshot outperform BTC and 32 outperform ETH.

The small-tail median return is about 0.94%, below BTC and ETH. Its 14.19% equal-weight mean is heavily distorted by the approximately 583% A7A5 observation and is not evidence of broad small-cap leadership.
Negative settled ETF flows and declining stablecoin supply constrain the case for durable continuation without proving that the current rebound must immediately fail.
